content:
kevin: Heads-up — a large customer (acme) reported repeated 429s on embeddings while chat and streaming stayed healthy. Looks like their embeddings jobs are exhausting the shared token quota.

maria: Are the 429s coming from the token limiter or the request limiter?

kevin: Token limiter. We currently use a single token bucket per-org that covers all endpoints (chat/embeddings/rerank/streaming). Embeddings spike ate the bucket fast.

jen: We unified token accounting to avoid per-route complexity for billing, but this is the exact corner-case we worried about.

sam: Proposal: separate token buckets by endpoint-class (chat, embeddings, rerank, streaming). Also keep a small global reserve bucket for cross-endpoint bursts. That would prevent a heavy embeddings workload from starving low-latency chat.

aaron: Enforcement location question: do we enforce at edge (api-gateway), at routing layer, or at runtime on the serving instances? Edge is cheaper for wasted work but the gateway doesn't know token-level cost until parse. Runtime knows exact token count.

kevin: We could do a two-phase approach: cheap pre-check at gateway using estimated token cost (based on input length + heuristic) then final strict check at runtime using actual tokenized length. If gateway estimate exceeds soft limit, reject early with 429-soft and header X-Quota-Estimate.

maria: Console/UX note — if we split buckets we need to surface per-endpoint dashboards in the Console (token burn rate, burst headroom, per-key vs per-org). Otherwise support will be swamped.

jen: Agreed. Also need migration plan: 1) introduce per-endpoint counters in telemetry (no enforcement), 2) run soft-limits that log rejections but don't block, 3) enable hard enforcement behind org-level feature flag, 4) default on for new orgs.

sam: Example config I mocked for limit rules:
```yaml
quota_policies:
  per_org:
    default_global_tokens_per_min: 1_000_000
    per_endpoint:
      chat: 200_000
      embeddings: 600_000
      rerank: 100_000
      streaming: 100_000
    global_reserve: 50_000
```

kevin: Nice. We should also decide how to bill when we split — keep billing aligned to token usage but show per-endpoint consumption in invoices so customers can see where spend goes.

aaron: Redis token buckets are fine for now. For inner-loop scaled orgs we might need sharded token counters or token credits in an internal billing service. Also think about eventual-consistency windows for bursts across regions.

jen: Rollout plan: implement telemetry + gateway estimate in 2 weeks, enable soft-limits for 2 weeks to collect data, then enable hard enforcement behind flag. We'll add a per-org opt-out during the soft window.

ops-bot: poll created: "Split token buckets by endpoint class?" options: +1 (yes), -1 (no), :thinking:. Current reactions: +1 x2.

maria: For alerts — add a dashboard panel: "per-endpoint headroom" and an alert when headroom < 10% for >5m. Also a composite alert when global_reserve is hit.

kevin: Action items:
- sam: prototype gateway estimate + config parser (ETA 1 week)
- jen: Console work to add per-endpoint quota panels (ETA 2 weeks)
- aaron: validate Redis sharding approach for high-throughput tenants (ETA 2 weeks)
- ops: prepare soft-limit rollout runbook + customer comms (ETA 1 week)

kevin: tagging this for the 1.30 rollout planning doc. I'll start a short RFC with the config sketch and expected telemetry metrics.

maria: thanks — this should help avoid more surprise 429s for compute-heavy embedding jobs.

kevin: closing thread for now, will post RFC link once created.
